summary: Swap invariance was replaced by the strictly stronger requirement of support in the symmetric subspace.

original.context: V is the isometry onto A tensor Sym^2(B), of dimension 3 times 6 = 18. The frozen task asked for an extension invariant under swapping two qutrit B systems, not necessarily supported only in their symmetric subspace.

witness.explanation: Swap invariance was replaced by the strictly stronger requirement of support in the symmetric subspace.
witness.evidence: Let v=(|01>-|10>)/sqrt(2) and X=|0><0|_A tensor |v><v|. X is positive semidefinite and obeys S X S=X because Sv=-v. It is therefore swap-invariant, but its support lies entirely in the antisymmetric B sector and cannot be written V rho V^T. In the qutrit case the omitted block has dimension 3 times 3 = 9. The code solves a restricted feasibility problem, so its infeasibility cannot certify the original criterion.
